I downloaded last version fo camtrapR from Github

Error in filterRecordTable(recordTable = Asilvestrado, minDeltaTime = 30,  :

The recordTable comes from an Excel file read in R. This file has all the fields that are delivered with the recordTable() function.

Tried different formats of date and time in base R and the same

I attach an example subset

Any thoughts?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: Announcement: new function for filtering record tables
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Re: Announcement: new function for filtering record tables
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The problem is that you quote the value for parameter recordTable

recordTable = "TES21_SpatialTag1and2",

That makes it a character value instead of a data.frame. Try removing the quotes first and make sure that TES21_SpatialTag1and2
Is a data frame.
Best,
Jürgen

Hi,
camtrapR is currently not available on CRAN, so the PDF manual is also not available there. I'd recommend using the documentation in R with
?functionName
until a new version is published.

The PDF manual will be available again when a new version is available on CRAN.
Best regards,
Jürgen

I would appreciate some help. Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
can you please share the data structure of the agouti export? Then I can provide some guidance.
Generally I'd expect something analogous to the camera trap table and record table from camtrapR, and then it is mostly a matter of telling camtrapR which columns to use for what (since the default column names used by camtrapR most likely won't match the Agouti export).
I think Agouti can export to camtrapDP format. That would likely be the easiest option.
Anyways, please provide some more detail.
Thank you

Hello,
Thank you for the answer. Finally I managed to start analyses. The data format was camtrapDP with a .json file, and 3 .csv media, observations and deployments files all exported from Agouti.
I used camtraptor on R studio to open the .json file and managed to create a record table from this file with all independent observations from the cameras (I chose 30min as a limit to have independent observations of the same species).
Now I am working on species accumulation curves using the package iNEXT to plot species accumulation with camera days. I have some issues to organize the data as I have 7 sites, each site has a different amount of cameras and each camera has a different deployment time (accumulated camera days). I started to make accumulation curves for each camera. For example, for the site 1, I have 9 cameras. I generated 9 accumulation curves, but I would like to have like a mean curve for all these 9 cameras.
I tried to organize my data as a matrix of incidence frequencies : the first number is the total number of camera days for each camera, the second number is the incidence frequency of species 1, then species 2 etc. (data format for https://chao.shinyapps.io/iNEXTOnline/)

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] removing DA species from the plots of a CommunityModel
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] removing DA species from the plots of a CommunityModel
messages.body_plain:
Please try with the dev branch on GitHub:
remotes::install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", ref = "dev", build_vignettes = TRUE)
plot_coef and plot_effects both have a new argument "subsetSpecies". Include all species that you wish to show in that argument. The default is to show all species.

In the plot you shared something is clearly wrong, but I can't say for sure without seeing the code you used. I hope the new version provides a solution for you though.

On a side note, a quick and dirty solution (and generally not advisable) is to subset the underlying data of the plot object itself. For example (using an example from the vignette):
test <-  plot_effects(mod.jags,
                      fit.jags,
                      submodel = "state")
test$utm_y$data <- test$utm_y$data[test$utm_y$data$Species %in% c("EGY", "VTA"),]
test$utm_y

But in general it is better to filter before plotting, which is what the subsetSpecies arguments mentioned above do.

messages.subject: camtrapR 2.3.0 released on CRAN
messages.subject_clean: camtrapR 2.3.0 released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
camtrapR 2.3.0 was released on CRAN:
New features:
Shiny dashboard for data exploration and analysis (surveyDashboard).
Temporal filtering of record tables (filterRecordTable).
Support for Royle-Nichols models in community occupancy models
Enhanced predict function with output types and batch processing.
Species richness information from communityModel (JAGS only).
Bug fixes:
Addresses last camera operation and ProblemX column issues.
Corrects errors in prediction and effects plots.
Other changes:
removed goodness of fit statistics from community model results (pending some checks, will be moved to standalone function in upcoming release)
Migrates dependencies, removes rgdal, and updates plot titles.
For details see the NEWS <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/news/news.html>.

As usual install via:
install.packages("camtrapR")

There is also a dev version on GitHub which contains a new function createCovariates (for extracting covariate values from rasters and creating prediction rasters). Install via:
# install.packages("remotes")
# install.packages("R.rsp")
remotes::install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR",ref = "dev", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: Create a record table with camtrapR from agouti files
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
you don't need the images, instead you can simply use the record table (observationData) as a basis for further analyses, such as activity or occupancy. It contains all the relevant information (location, date/time, species). If necessary you can filter the record table to only contain independent records using filterRecordTable().
If you can be more specific about the type of analysis you wish to conduct and the attempts you made then it would be easier to provide guidance.
Best regards,
